newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup sees possible Sabena measures.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup sees possible Sabena measures.

text.p: SAirGroup said it had taken precautionary provisions of 300 million Swiss francs in its 1996 accounts to cover various possible future measures, including further measures at Belgian partner Sabena SA.

SAirGroup chief executive Philippe Bruggisser told the company's annual news conference that there were no specific plans to use the provisions right now, but he expected tougher times in Europe's liberalised airline market and the provisions were taken to give SAirGroup room to manoeuvre.
"We want to -- we have to -- positively improve our costs in a decisive manner," Bruggisser said, adding:
"Maybe we have to take further hard measures to remain competitive. But I don't know when."
Bruggisser also said the provisions could be used in the event cooperation with its partner airlines was strengthened, one its goals. Another reason was Sabena.

SAirGroup owns 49.5 percent of Sabena and fully wrote down the value of its stake in Sabena in 1996 -- 267 million francs -- reflecting the airline's 1996 loss of 8.9 billion Belgian francs and an expected loss in 1997.
"It is possible -- we can't exclude it -- that further measures at Sabena will be necessary," Bruggisser said, adding such measures could not just be financed out of pocket.
He stressed there were no specific measures for Sabena planned, but he noted that Sabena was also faced with replacing its fleet of Boeing 737 aircraft in coming years.
Bruggisser said he was expecting Sabena to "massively improve" its result in 1997 and the goal was to return to profitability in 1998.
"If Sabena is far away from its target in 1997 then we will have to consider what to do. However, it would be wrong to speculate over this after only three months," he added.
In 1996 SAirGroup had net extraordinary charges of 698 million francs, pushing the group into a net loss of 497 million francs.
The charges include 300 million francs in precautionary provisions, 267 million for the Sabena writedown and a further 172 million to cover various provisions.

Chief financial officer Georges Schorderet said the 172 million francs covered 50 million in goodwill depreciations, 40 million for interest rate and currency swaps and 80 million to cover a wide variety of possible charges at subsidiaries.
In 1995 SAirGroup took extraordinary charges of 366 million francs, partially to cover the reduction of some 2,000 jobs at the Swissair parent company.

The cost of early retirement for 700 positions amounted to 190 million francs and separation packages fo 440 positions cost 40 million for total cost of 230 million. Some 800 positions were cut through natural attrition.
